planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded while the vine climbs into sun.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a trellis or fence. Multi Blue produces unusual, fully double flowers in rich blue-purple, the outer sepals surrounding a dense pompom of shorter, twisted, spiky inner petaloids that give each bloom a shaggy, almost anemone-like texture unlike the flat, single flowers of most clematis. It flowers in late spring to early summer on old wood with a possible lighter rebloom on new growth, so prune only lightly to remove dead or weak stems in late winter rather than cutting the vine back hard. Its unusual double form makes it a conversation-piece specimen for a trellis, arbor, or large container support.

common_name: Polish Spirit Clematis (Vigorous Deep Purple Viticella Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Polish Spirit blooms on new growth, so it can be pruned back hard each late winter.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a trellis or fence. Polish Spirit is a vigorous, free-flowering viticella-type clematis producing masses of rich, velvety deep purple flowers with a lighter central boss of cream-colored stamens, blooming heavily from midsummer into fall on a fast-growing vine that can cover a large trellis or scramble through a shrub or small tree in a single season. Because it flowers entirely on new growth, it belongs to the group of clematis that should be pruned hard, back to about a foot from the ground, in late winter, which keeps it vigorous and full of bloom rather than tangled and bare at the base. Its viticella parentage also gives it good resistance to clematis wilt, a fungal disease that troubles some large-flowered hybrid clematis.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Rooguchi has a scrambling rather than strongly climbing habit and benefits from being tied loosely to a support or allowed to weave through companion shrubs.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs or scrambles into full sun to light shade. Rooguchi is a distinctive Japanese viticella-type hybrid bearing nodding, bell-shaped, thick-petaled flowers in deep purple-blue with a paler, twisted, recurved petal tip, a form entirely different from the flat, open flowers of most large-flowered clematis, blooming continuously from early summer into fall. Its lax, semi-climbing habit works well trained on a low trellis or obelisk, woven through a shrub, or left to sprawl at the front of a border, and unlike many clematis it flowers on new growth, so it can be cut back hard in late winter. Its long, prolific bloom season and unusual flower form have made it a favorite among clematis collectors and gardeners looking for something different from the typical large-flowered hybrids.

common_name: Betty Corning Clematis (Fragrant Pale Lavender Bell Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Betty Corning blooms on new growth, so it can be pruned back hard each late winter.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a trellis or fence. Betty Corning, discovered as a chance seedling in a New York garden in the 1930s, bears delicate, nodding, bell-shaped flowers in soft pale lavender with gently recurved petal tips and a light, sweet fragrance, blooming over an unusually long season from early summer well into fall. Its refined, understated flowers and fragrance set it apart from the bolder, flatter blooms of large-flowered hybrid clematis, and because it flowers on new growth it can be cut back hard in late winter without sacrificing bloom, a more forgiving pruning regime than many older clematis cultivars require.

common_name: Snow White Indian Hawthorn (Compact White-Flowered Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring, summer, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Snow White is a compact Indian hawthorn cultivar producing abundant clusters of pure white flowers in spring, followed by small blue-black berries that attract birds, all on a dense, rounded mound of glossy, leathery, disease-resistant foliage. Its low, tidy habit fits foundation plantings, low borders, and coastal landscape beds, and it shares the species' outstanding tolerance for salt spray, wind, heat, and poor sandy soils, making it a dependable performer in exposed Gulf Coast sites. Good air circulation between plants helps minimize the leaf spot disease that can affect Indian hawthorn in humid conditions.

common_name: Eleanor Tabor Indian Hawthorn (Deep Pink Compact Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring, summer, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Eleanor Tabor bears an unusually heavy flush of deep pink flowers each spring, richer in color than many Indian hawthorn cultivars, on a dense, rounded shrub with glossy, leathery, disease-resistant evergreen foliage followed by small blue-black berries that draw birds. Its bold spring color and dependable form make it a strong choice for foundation plantings, low hedges, and coastal landscape beds. Like other Indian hawthorn cultivars, it tolerates salt spray, wind, heat, and poor sandy soils well; provide good air circulation between plants to help minimize leaf spot disease in humid climates.

common_name: Pinkie Indian Hawthorn (Classic Compact Pink Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring, summer, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Pinkie is one of the oldest and most widely planted Indian hawthorn cultivars, a garden standard for decades, bearing soft pink flower clusters in spring above dense, glossy, leathery evergreen foliage, followed by small blue-black berries that attract birds. Its low, mounding, compact habit fits foundation plantings and low hedges, and it shares the species' reliable tolerance for salt spray, wind, heat, and poor sandy soils, a long-proven performer in coastal Gulf landscapes. Good air circulation between plants helps minimize the leaf spot disease that can affect Indian hawthorn in humid conditions.

common_name: Georgia Charm Indian Hawthorn (Compact Rose-Pink Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring, summer, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Georgia Charm produces rose-pink flower clusters in spring above compact, dense, glossy evergreen foliage, followed by small blue-black berries that attract birds, on a tidy, rounded shrub sized for smaller foundation plantings and low hedges. Like other Indian hawthorn cultivars, it tolerates salt spray, wind, heat, and poor sandy soils well, making it a dependable choice for coastal Gulf Coast landscapes. Good air circulation between plants helps minimize the leaf spot disease that can affect Indian hawthorn in humid conditions; established plants need little care beyond occasional shaping.

common_name: Silver Waves Camellia (Large Ruffled White Anemone-Form Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall in well-drained, acidic (pH 5.5–6.5), humus-rich, moist soil in partial shade.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, strongly acidic (pH 5.5–6.5), humus-rich soil in partial shade. Silver Waves is an Award of Garden Merit-winning camellia bearing large, semi-double to anemone-form flowers of pure white with gently ruffled, wavy-edged petals surrounding a center of golden stamens, a bold, textured flower form that stands out among the many flatter-petaled white camellia cultivars. It flowers over a long midseason window on a vigorous, well-branched shrub with the glossy, dark-green foliage typical of Camellia japonica. Its large, distinctive flowers make it a strong specimen or accent planting; prune, if needed, immediately after bloom in late winter or early spring, before next year's flower buds set.
